name: BYRNES, Alison

headline.note: The documented career consists of full-time party employment, political staff work, study and elected office, all excluded from the two headline sectors under the codebook. Earlier political-staff transition dates and the 2002–2005 period remain unresolved; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Byrnes states that after leaving school in year 11 she completed a business administration course and obtained her first full-time job as NSW Labor's accountant's assistant. She told ABC she started working for Labor at 16; with her official birth year this supports 1990 at year precision. Her first speech says she commuted for a year and a half, but calendar endpoints are not published, so no end date is imposed.
career_spells.counting_note: Employment by a party organisation is excluded from public/private headline totals.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Stephen Martin MP (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: Her first speech says she moved to Stephen Martin's office after one and a half years at NSW Labor and describes electorate work as the next job. It does not state the appointment or cessation dates, payroll entity, hours or leave. Martin represented Macarthur and later Cunningham, but his service dates are not substituted for Byrnes's employment dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Sharon Bird MP (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: A legitimately public LinkedIn search result separates an executive-assistant role in 2005–2007 from the later adviser role. Byrnes's first speech independently confirms 17 years in Bird's electorate and ministerial offices, while ABC confirms she still worked for Bird in February 2022. Exact dates, payroll entity, hours and leave remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Sharon Bird MP (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official biography records senior policy and media adviser work from 2005 to 2022. The public LinkedIn result refines the senior role to July 2007–March 2022 and lists the prior executive-assistant position separately. Her first speech confirms work across Bird's electorate and ministerial offices but does not identify when office context, title or payroll changed. Hours, leave and any campaign break remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary and party biographies identify the qualification and institution. Byrnes says it followed a sizeable study gap, but the enrolment/completion dates, load and overlap with employment are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current official biographies establish House service from 21 May 2022. Committee or parliamentary duties are nested within this elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.
